title: Lane-speed per-mille scaling makes Standard/Best packets vanish before the arrival node — no end-to-end ride
detail: frac is scaled by ppm/1000 (Standard 850, Best 700), but packets are culled at true progress 1.0 — Standard/Best packets visually vanish at 85%/70% of the edge, never riding end-to-end as the spec and demo claim. Express (1000) is the only lane that visually arrives.
recommended_fix: Do not scale the along-edge fraction; render full-length positions and encode lane speed as a per-tick motion-rate readout, or normalize ppm so every lane visually reaches the arrival node.

title: Spec E22: Always section and I/O matrix disagree on admission when the arrival's lane is empty
evidence:
Always section: "- **E22 spawn guard** inside `flow_spawn`: at `pool_max_packets`, the same ladder over in-flight packets (lane = on-edge → `qos_lane_of(its pipe)`, else class `default_lane`); the arriving packet drops when its lane is the shed target."

I/O matrix: "| E22 pool | pool at `pool_max_packets`; spawn arrives | the ladder sheds the lowest-priority non-empty lane's newest; the arrival is admitted ONLY when that target is STRICTLY lower priority than its own lane, else the arrival drops (the inversion guard — an Express resident never pays for a Standard arrival) | n/a |"

Change log: "(a) E22's shed rule was `shed_lane != arrive_lane` — priority-inverting ... corrected to STRICTLY-lower-priority-only (`shed_lane > arrive_lane`) + a pin (Case C)."
detail: With an empty arrival lane and only higher-priority lanes non-empty (e.g., Best arrival, Best queue empty, Standard/Express full), Always admits (its lane is not the shed target) but the I/O matrix drops (target not strictly lower). Frozen spec contradicts itself; the change log confirms the strict rule is the correction.
recommended_fix: Reword the Always E22 bullet to the strict rule: the arrival is admitted only when the shed target's lane is strictly lower priority than the arrival's lane.

title: data/palette.json not updated in this diff — lane_speeds always resolves via the fallback branch
detail: The new per-mille lane-speed readout is never driven by data — every app/demo run takes the {1000,850,700} fallback, and the loader's parse branch is dead until the key ships. Behavior is safe, but the data-driven intent is unmet in this wave.
recommended_fix: Add lane_speeds: [1000, 850, 700] to data/palette.json in this wave, or drop the loader branch and document the readout as code-constant.
